title: Umbrage Energy: edge onramp notes
content:
Context:
- Small utility provider (Umbrage Energy) wants an on-prem/edge inference pop-up for transformer-based triage assistant at distributed substations.
- Primary goals: 250ms P95 local response for short prompts (<=128 tokens), low egress (air-gap-friendly), predictable cost for months of operation.

What we heard on call (raw):
- "We can't have cloud egress for PII - only periodic rollout bundles via secure USB" — security team emphasis.
- Fleet is heterogeneous: Dell R740x (on-prem racks) + a couple of Jetson/ARM edge nodes for remote sites.
- Primary workload: call transcription + triage prompt -> short structured JSON output.
- Offline periods are common (satellite comms), so model must degrade gracefully.

Initial technical constraints / gotchas:
- No GPU at ~60% of sites. For CPU-only: 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM. Need a lightweight model fallback (quantized) and runtime check to pick it.
- Network MTU drops on satellite links — large KV cache fetches can stall; prefer prefix caching with small chunks.
- KMS/HSM: customer will only accept hardware-backed keys for private key ops. Integrations limited to PKCS11.
- Admins want deterministic startup: avoid JIT comp steps on first inference in tight windows. Precompile kernels during packaging.

Serving plan idea (sketch):
- Packaging: two artifacts per site: (1) high-perf model bundle for racks with GPUs (FP16 + q4_0), (2) CPU-optimized quantized variant (int8-ish) with small vocab subset for remote sites.
- Runtime: Redwood Private shim that runs in air-gapped mode, local control plane, with Canary upgrade via signed bundles (USB import).
- Caching: Local prefix cache with LRU and per-prompt TTL, max cache item size 4KB.
- Fallbacks: If KV cache miss + no GPU, route to tiny 2-layer quantized LM to keep latency <500ms.

Measurements to capture during trial:
- cold start time (binary present, first token)
- P50/P95 per-site for typical triage prompt (30–80 tokens output)
- memory usage under sustained burst (60 concurrent tiny requests)
- number of bundle imports per quarter (security audit metric)

Open questions / actions for next sync:
- (Aisha) confirm exact HW on 12 pilot sites by 2025-02-20 (Jordan to help).
- (Samir) check PKCS11 flows we currently support and list missing drivers (due 2025-02-17).
- Ask security: are signed bundles sufficient or do they require remote attestation (TPM) on device?
- Prototype: ship a CPU quantized toy package to one Jetson-equivalent and measure 95th latency. Target: <500ms.

Notes from quick prototype run (yesterday):
- Built int8 quantized Llama-variant with reduced embeddings. On 8vCPU/32G VM: P95 ~720ms for 64-token output. Memory 12GB. Needs further perf work (kernel selection and smaller vocab).
- Prefix caching reduced token work by ~30% on repeated prompts in test set. Good sign.

Risks / non-starters:
- Heavy reliance on USB bundle process — operationally clunky for many sites. Need a validated offline OTA pattern.
- On-device model updates tied to security approval cycles could lag and cause regressions. Recommend staged canary with rollback.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Share lightweight packaging checklist + precompile script (Aisha).
- Samir to list PKCS11 driver matrix and any HSM vendor gaps.
- Schedule 30-min lab run with their infra team to drop a CPU bundle onto a candidate site (target Fri 2025-02-21).
- Draft a short runbook for USB bundle import, verification steps, and rollback (deliverable by Mon 2025-02-24).

Quick personal thoughts (scratch):
- Could we exploit model surgery to prune task-specific heads (triage-only) for remote sites? Might squeeze latency.
- Consider using a tiny local rule-based fallback for critical safety outputs when offline and model uncertain.

Last call notes snippet (raw transcript bits):
- "If it's under 500ms we can consider pushing to prod" — Ops lead
- "We need the device to be auditable for at least 12 months" — Security

---
End of scratchpad. Keep lean; this will be handed to delivery team for quick triage run.
